what: Two videos posted on X show a man posing as a former student of James Talarico and falsely accusing him of sexually assaulting him in 2012; researchers judged the videos 'very likely' deepfakes.
who_made_it: Russia-aligned influence operation Storm-1516, per Graphika ('high confidence') and Clemson's Darren Linvill; posted by the new X account @zyon_lewis_5, which impersonated a real former student
how_caught: Graphika and NewsGuard flagged lips out of sync with the audio, stiff faces and no body movement, plus AI-detection results; the real man told Lead Stories it was not him; PolitiFact rated it Pants on Fire; X suspended the account by Oct 22

what: An AI-generated video of four Black residents, one of them a Wong poll worker, praising interim county judge Daniel Wong for giving them jobs was shared on Facebook.
target: Voters; it promoted Daniel Wong (R) against Dexter McCoy (D)
who_made_it: Shared by Wong's campaign page and the Fort Bend Republican Party; the campaign says, without naming anyone, that 'a Democrat' made it
how_caught: Commenters noticed warped backgrounds and clothing and the same-sounding voice for all four speakers; the campaign then took it down

what: An AI-generated video showed Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith running away from reporters who were asking about her healthcare vote; it was captioned 'Based on a true story.'
who_made_it: Scott Colom's (D) Senate campaign, on Facebook and Instagram
how_caught: The state Republican Party complained. AG Lynn Fitch said the video 'appears to violate' Mississippi's political deepfake law and set a removal deadline. Colom called it parody but took it down on Oct 23

what: Two attack ads used AI-generated images of state Rep. Vikki Goodwin at a University of Texas football game wearing a shirt reading 'taxes' instead of 'Texas'.
target: Vikki Goodwin (D), Lt. Governor nominee; the ads also attacked James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa
who_made_it: Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick's (R) campaign; a spokesperson called them 'obvious parody produced to entertain'
how_caught: Goodwin said she never did or said what the ads show and filed a criminal complaint under Texas's election deepfake law with the Travis County Sheriff on Sept 19; Patrick deleted both videos

what: AI-made video clips showed actors and musicians, among them Robert De Niro, Julia Roberts and Cher, attacking Democrats; some pushed the hashtag #AllDemocratsAreCriminals, and many other clips made false corruption claims against Democratic candidates.
target: The Democratic Party and Democratic candidates; the celebrities' likenesses
who_made_it: Russian state-backed operation Matryoshka (also called Operation Overload), per social media researchers cited by Bloomberg
reach: Bloomberg reports that bots were used to inflate view counts; no totals given
how_caught: Social media researchers cited by Bloomberg. The clips began appearing on X in early September

what: A series of ads uses AI renderings of Sen. Jon Ossoff getting hair and beauty treatments in a salon, with the line 'Jon Ossoff talks pretty, his actions ugly.'
who_made_it: Senate Leadership Fund (super PAC aligned with Senate Republicans)
how_caught: Reporters identified the AI renderings. The ads carry no AI label, and Georgia law does not require one. Ossoff called them 'deepfake videos used to fabricate political advertising' and said they 'should come down immediately'

what: A campaign ad uses AI to depict James Talarico defacing a Bible with crayon, with the line 'In the beginning God was non-binary.'
how_caught: Identified in an Axios review of AI political ads. Talarico said he had tried to ban AI deepfakes in campaigns 'because they are misleading'

what: Super PAC ads show a fabricated family photo of Abdul El-Sayed with podcaster Hasan Piker and four women in niqabs, and an AI scene of him playing a Risk-style game with cards reading 'Death to America' and 'Celebrate 9/11'.
how_caught: The family-photo ad carries a written and spoken AI disclosure. The group says the ads are 'grounded in El-Sayed's own public statements'

what: An ad shows an AI version of Gov. Josh Shapiro talking about taxes, abortion and data centers and 'admitting' he fast-tracked data centers after taking $5 million in contributions.
how_caught: The ad itself says it was made with AI. Shapiro's spokesperson called it 'cheap, dishonest AI' (expletive)

what: A series of campaign ads uses AI versions of Gov. Kathy Hochul, including one billed as 'what a truthful Kathy Hochul ad would look like', in which a man outside a police precinct asks her 'Want some crack?', and earlier ads showing her gardening with NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani.
how_caught: Some of the ads carry AI notices, but how clearly varies. In August the state Democratic Party filed a complaint with the state Board of Elections alleging that some lacked the labels state law requires; Blakeman calls them satire

what: Several AI deepfakes of Democrat Zach Dembo, including one of him staring into the camera, ran in ads boosting Republican Ralph Alvarado.
who_made_it: No Going Back PAC, backed by MAGA Inc.
how_caught: Identified in an Axios review. Dembo: 'I did not expect them to lie about my appearance'

race: Wisconsin US House (Rep. Derrick Van Orden's seat)
what: An AI-generated video, posted on X in August, shows Democratic challenger Rebecca Cooke saying she wants to 'take advantage of as much corruption as possible and give every illegal alien free healthcare', which she never said.
who_made_it: Rep. Derrick Van Orden (R), via his X account
how_caught: Cooke's lawyers sent a cease-and-desist letter. Van Orden replied with an AI video of a duck saying 'cease and desist'. No removal is reported

what: An AI-generated video shows state Sen. Cathy Kipp as a grocery cashier who pockets customers' change 'to help educate children', attacking the ballot measure she sponsored.
how_caught: The video admits near the end that it is AI but lacks the formal disclaimer. Kipp filed the first complaint under Colorado's deepfake disclosure law; the Secretary of State's elections division is investigating, and the Institute calls it satire

what: An attack ad uses AI-generated video that appears manipulated from Democrat Jamie Ager's own barn-dance campaign ad: a pride flag is added to the wall and plainclothes dancers are replaced with drag performers while children watch. It closes: 'Jamie Ager talks like you and me on TV, but he's dancing with they/them.'
who_made_it: Republican Jennifer Balkcom's campaign (approved the ad); paid for by the National Republican Congressional Committee
how_caught: A News & Observer fact check found the footage appears manipulated from Ager's own ad and carries no AI disclaimer; North Carolina has no disclosure law. Asheville drag performers Divine Holeburn and Nova say their AI-generated likenesses were used without permission and sent cease-and-desist letters. Ager called it '100% fake AI-generated'. The NRCC stands by the ad and did not say whether it disclosed AI use
source_label: News & Observer fact check (via Yahoo), Oct 24; WLOS, Oct 26

what: A newscast-style video uses photos of Haya Akbik, who interned for Sherrod Brown years ago, and other former staffers to attribute allegations to them; Akbik says the claims attributed to her are 'completely made up'.
who_made_it: Likely Russia's Storm-1516 network, per Clemson's Darren Linvill (the accounts had shared earlier Storm-1516 content)
reach: Copies still online Oct 27, some with 'hundreds of shares' (AP); X removed the originals
how_caught: Dartmouth's Hany Farid said it was likely generated or manipulated with AI, a 'fairly low-tech fake'; Akbik denied the claims; X suspended the accounts
